solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Strike breaker goes back to achieve objective

indicators.note: going back means the strike breaker's word is read from right to left

parts.note: a rat is slang for a worker who breaks a strike
to achieve something is to get it

explanation.surface: A scab returns to work in order to reach some goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike breaker' reads like a description of the whole clue's subject, but it is a slang word for a scab, turned round by 'goes back'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an objective is the goal you aim at.

clue.text: End of the road for miners involved with trade union

indicators.note: involved suggests tangled together, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Mineworkers joining their union marks the end of the line for them.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminus is the final stop on a route, literally where a road or line ends.

clue.text: Trustworthy person who stops boat sinking after capsize on deserted lake

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece
after a capsize the boat is upside down, so in this down clue the word is turned over

parts.note: a bailer scoops water out of a boat to keep it afloat

indicators.note: deserted means emptied, leaving only the outside letters of lake

explanation.surface: Someone bailing desperately after their boat overturns on an empty lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after capsize' is the turnaround signal for this down clue, and 'deserted' leaves only the ends of lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something trustworthy can be depended on.

clue.text: Right for the old to be upset over surrender

indicators.note: over here means one piece sits around and covers the other
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: ye is an old form of the
to quit is to give up or surrender

explanation.surface: Elderly people are upset at being made to give something up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be upset' turns YE into EY, which goes 'over' QUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: In law equity means fairness or a right, as in a shareholder's stake or natural justice.

clue.text: A strike in the heart of London causes disaster

indicators.note: in means the first pieces go inside the next one

parts.note: the City is London's historic centre and financial district
to lam is to beat or strike

explanation.surface: A transport strike in central London causes chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The heart of London' looks like the middle letter D, but it is the City.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a calamity is a disaster or catastrophe.

clue.text: Engaged in insane warfare again

indicators.note: engaged in means contained within, so the letters are held inside the phrase

explanation.surface: A country fights in mad warfare once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to do something anew is to do it again, afresh.

clue.text: Usual to say yes to newspaper boss

parts.note: to say yes to an offer is to accept it
ED is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: It is normal to agree with the editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an accepted practice is the customary or usual one.

clue.text: Failing business goes under at home

indicators.note: in a down clue, going under means placed below the other piece

parts.note: in means at home
a firm is a business

explanation.surface: A struggling company collapses while the owner sits at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes under' looks like the definition of failing, but it places FIRM below IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone infirm is weak or failing in health.

clue.text: Unknown 50% misspelled "screamed"

parts.note: in algebra y is an unknown quantity

indicators.note: fifty per cent means half, here the second half of the word misspelled

explanation.surface: A note complains that an unknown person spelt 'screamed' wrong half the time.
explanation.walkthrough: The back half of misspelled is ELLED, after Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to have yelled is to have screamed or shouted.

clue.text: Europe centrally has influence over high risk betting system

indicators.note: centrally means take the middle letters of Europe
over means the word is turned round

parts.note: to have pull is to have influence

explanation.surface: Europe's central powers sway a dangerous gambling scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the influence word round in this across clue; the definition is the long phrase at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll-up is an accumulator bet where each winning stake rolls on to the next race, so risk mounts.

clue.text: Forgiving about foul crime after nothing is lost

indicators.note: about signals the letters are turned about and rearranged, once one of them is lost

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Being lenient about a dreadful offence once nothing is lost.
explanation.walkthrough: Take O from FOUL CRIME and rearrange what is left; 'is lost' signals the removal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a merciful person shows clemency and forgives.

clue.text: Mean to declare how old you are

parts.note: to aver is to declare
your age is how old you are

explanation.surface: Someone intends to admit their age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like a verb, intend, but it is the statistical noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the mean is the arithmetic average.

clue.text: During performance I have to be quiet

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'
an act is a performance
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: An actor told to keep silent while on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something inactive is idle or quiet, doing nothing.

clue.text: Rare for solver initially to work out breakdown of clue

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of solver

parts.note: to parse is to break a sentence or clue into its parts

explanation.surface: It is unusual for a solver to analyse a clue at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: sparse means thinly scattered, scarce or rare.

clue.text: Post Office raised online price of work

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means turned upward, reading bottom to top

parts.note: E stands for electronic, as in e-mail
a rate is a price

explanation.surface: The Post Office has put up its online prices for a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a machine that works is said to operate.

clue.text: Nasty judge regularly gets extremely lonely

indicators.note: regularly means take every other letter of judge
extremely means take the outermost letters of lonely

explanation.surface: An unpleasant judge often becomes very isolated.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an ugly scene or mood is nasty or threatening.

clue.text: Slip through as a visitor

parts.note: to trip is to slip or stumble
per means through or by, as in 'per post'

explanation.surface: A guest stumbles on their way through the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A day tripper is a short-term visitor or tourist.

clue.text: Broke embargo on Scandinavian currency over time

parts.note: an embargo is a ban
KR abbreviates the krona or krone of Sweden, Norway and Denmark
up means over or finished, as in 'time is up'

explanation.surface: A trade ban on Swedish money has run on so long it ruined someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to be broke is to have no money, insolvent.

clue.text: Kill foreigner with the other hand finally pushed slightly forward

indicators.note: the new letter is shifted one place towards the front
the final letter stands for right, and the other hand is left, so one is swapped for the other

parts.note: a stranger is a foreigner or outsider

explanation.surface: A murderer kills an outsider by edging the left hand forward.
explanation.walkthrough: R (right) at the end becomes L (left), giving STRANGEL; moving that L one place forward gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Strangling is a way of killing by choking, so it is a specific kind of kill.

clue.text: Gut reaction isn't out of place in court

indicators.note: out of place means the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: An outburst in court is inappropriate, a lawyer feels in their gut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' gives its own letters rather than signalling a container; 'out of place' scrambles isn't.
explanation.definitionFit: Instinct is an intuitive, unreasoned response, which is what a gut reaction is.

clue.text: Set including outrageous gag is wasted

indicators.note: including means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: set concrete is hard

indicators.note: outrageous suggests wildly out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A TV show that included a scandalous joke now looks finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like a noun but means solid, as concrete sets; 'outrageous' scrambles the joke word.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a haggard face looks gaunt and wasted from exhaustion.

clue.text: Shock arrest after model goes missing

indicators.note: going missing means the model letter disappears from the word

parts.note: to stunt growth is to arrest it
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: An arrest is shocking once a fashion model vanishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to stun someone is to shock or stupefy them.

clue.text: Is a composer of liturgies we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals the word is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: rites are forms of religious ceremony, liturgies

explanation.surface: Someone composes church services, people report.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who writes is composing, so 'is a composer' describes the action.

clue.text: Make the first pair of obsolescent lichens germinate

indicators.note: the first pair of means the opening two letters of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: Forcing ageing lichens to sprout.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to oblige someone to do something is to make or compel them.

clue.text: Easy to manage first person in position

indicators.note: in means the first person goes inside the other word

parts.note: to plant is to place or position
I is the first person pronoun

explanation.surface: A first person in a role who is easy to handle.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone pliant bends easily to others, so is easily managed.

clue.text: Take to task about UK invading the outskirts of Belgrade

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: invading means going inside the other piece
outskirts are the outer edges, so the first and last letters of Belgrade

parts.note: UK is taken as written

explanation.surface: Criticising Britain for invading the suburbs of the Serbian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to take someone to task is to scold or reprimand them.

clue.text: Loyal supporter resolved last conflict with Tory leader

indicators.note: resolved here means broken down and solved again, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: war is conflict

indicators.note: the leader of Tory is its first letter

explanation.surface: A loyal party member settled the last war under a Conservative leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' rearranges LAST to STAL. A Tory is a British Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalwart is a dependable, faithful backer of a cause or party.

clue.text: Cop ultimately gets to do a deal

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of cop

parts.note: to act is to do something

explanation.surface: A police officer finally agrees to make a bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a pact is an agreement or deal.

clue.text: Panel of judges bother about the point retrospectively

indicators.note: about means the first word goes around the other

parts.note: a trial is a nuisance or bother

indicators.note: retrospectively means looking back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the nub is the central point

explanation.surface: A bench of judges fussing over a matter after the event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bother' here is a noun, a trying nuisance; 'retrospectively' reads the point word backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribunal is a body appointed to adjudicate, a panel of judges.

clue.text: Starts to mount armed resistance against soldier on northern border

indicators.note: starts means the first letters of the next three words

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Rebels begin an armed uprising against troops on the northern frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a margin is an edge or border.

clue.text: Watch police state collapse after oil disappears

indicators.note: collapse suggests falling into pieces, so what is left gets rearranged

explanation.surface: Seeing an authoritarian regime fall once its oil runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: Take O, I, L from POLICE STATE and rearrange the rest; 'disappears' signals the removal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to spectate is to watch an event as an onlooker.

clue.text: Army corps goes in to restore highway

indicators.note: goes in means the corps sits inside the other word

parts.note: stet is the proofreader's mark meaning restore a deletion
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Army engineers move in to repair a main road.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a street is a public road or highway.
